source_record.native_common_basis: Decision-relevant feasible alternatives are retained only while learning and avoided reversal justify their cost and respect the real convergence deadline.
source_record.common_cost_and_alternative: Parallel exploration, prototypes, scarce skill, delay and loss of an expiring option count. A familiar reversible decision can choose one design with a fallback note.
attempted_contrary_interfaces: An option list treated as joint feasibility.
A confirming experiment rejected because the action remains unchanged.
A prototype treated as complete product qualification.
A partial input rejected for failing the whole receiver.
Sunk expenditure treated as future benefit.
Private cost preference treated as authority to waive a binding obligation.

positive_controls.argument: The uncertainty, required evidence and deadline identify which alternatives should remain open and what result would justify eliminating or confirming one.
Architecture budgets, cross-cutting constraints and question-valid models delimit the feasible option set and identify consequential interactions before convergence.
A representative experiment result can eliminate an option or strengthen the warrant for retaining the present choice, even when the chosen action remains unchanged.
Actual decision rights, entrance evidence and commitment timing specify when an option may be eliminated or must be resolved rather than preserved indefinitely.
The real separable commitment and option-expiry structure determine which design alternatives can remain feasible and for how long.
Applicable obligations, permitted tailoring and adequate existing controls constrain the experiment or evidence needed before eliminating an option.
Demand, cost and lead-time ranges test whether preserving a particular option is affordable and whether delayed commitment risks losing its value.
Actual consequence, recovery, obligations and urgency define what evidence is needed before a feasible option can be committed or eliminated.
